scenarios.description: Escalating restrictions/blockade/conflict around Taiwan followed by partial supply-chain recovery; valuation-only action plan TAIWAN-S1..S3 is referenced but not used as model input.

probability_meta.rationale: Probability intentionally left to owner; calibration defines conditional outcomes only.

meta.rationale: Scenario is conditioned on onset of material restrictions at t0.
Material access friction without assuming full physical outage.
Cross-strait/export friction weakens China-linked revenue.
Near-term deployment caution offsets some substitution demand.
Packaging/memory logistics tighten.
Advanced packaging access becomes less reliable.
Near-term fab/equipment activity pauses before reconstruction response.
Risk-off financing shock.
Defense demand rises modestly.
Cross-strait supply and China access become more coupled.
AI capex becomes more dependent on semiconductor supply health.
Initial restrictions corresponding economically to legacy TAIWAN-S1; legacy actions are not model inputs.
Conditional seizure path assumes escalation from restrictions to blockade within roughly one to three quarters; timing is model uncertainty.
Large sustained supply-health shock.
Market-access/export shock.
Capacity deployment is constrained by unavailable compute inputs.
HBM supply becomes strongly constrained.
Advanced packaging becomes strongly constrained.
Equipment demand/shipments are disrupted before geographic substitution.
Global risk-off shock.
Defense procurement rises materially.
Blockade couples semiconductor supply and China market access.
AI infrastructure becomes supply constrained.
Funding and AI buildout co-move more strongly during blockade.
Economic analogue of legacy TAIWAN-S2; conditional on actual blockade.
Conflict timing is conditional on blockade and uncertain; no unconditional escalation probability is encoded here.
Extreme disruption to Taiwan-linked semiconductor supply.
Severe sanctions/market-access fragmentation.
Physical compute availability dominates demand willingness.
Severe HBM supply shock.
Severe packaging shock.
Equipment supply/demand shock during conflict.
Severe risk-off and financing stress.
War-economy procurement impulse.
Conflict links supply and sanctions/market access.
Compute investment becomes tightly supply constrained.
Financial and capex cycles become unusually coupled.
Economic analogue of legacy TAIWAN-S3; conditional on armed conflict.
Recovery onset is highly uncertain; six to sixteen quarters is a model-assumption range, not a forecast.
Supply remains structurally impaired even after acute conflict shock fades.
Sanctions/market fragmentation persist.
Replacement and sovereign compute buildout supports demand.
Memory supply partially normalizes.
Packaging partially normalizes.
Reconstruction/localization drives equipment demand.
Risk premium remains above BASE but acute stress fades.
Defense procurement remains elevated.
Persistent bifurcation remains after acute conflict.
AI capex remains more sensitive to supply health than BASE.
Recovery means partial normalization, not return to pre-shock geopolitics.

fact_catalog.signal: Official restrictions on shipping/airspace around Taiwan affecting commercial traffic.
fact_catalog.note: Legacy TAIWAN-S1 signal; action plan remains separate.

fact_catalog.signal: Effective blockade or sustained closure of principal commercial maritime/air routes.
fact_catalog.note: Requires observed restriction, not exercises alone.

fact_catalog.signal: Confirmed use of force / armed hostilities around Taiwan.
fact_catalog.note: Binary event for phase monitoring; does not encode owner action.

fact_catalog.signal: TSMC / key supplier production and shipment restoration or geographic substitution milestones.
fact_catalog.note: Used to judge whether recovery calibration requires revision.

notes: All magnitudes/timings are model_assumption unless explicitly fact-catalogued.

scenarios.description: US–China semiconductor technology race: Western subsidized capacity buildout, uncertain 3–5Y parity boundary, then persistent bifurcated production systems and accelerator price competition.

probability_meta.rationale: Owner explicitly requested separate probability judgment; calibration must not infer it.

meta.rationale: Scenario is conditioned on an ongoing strategic race at t0.
Western and Chinese fab buildout raises equipment cycle.
Sovereign localization accelerates.
Defense/strategic procurement rises.
AI infrastructure race sustains capex.
Power infrastructure buildout follows compute investment.
Fiscal/industrial investment pressure modestly raises rate environment.
Export controls mildly reduce cross-border addressability.
No physical Taiwan supply impairment is assumed before parity.
Compute service pricing not yet structurally reset.
Competition rises but parity has not yet been reached.
Compute and power buildout become more synchronized.
Capex race depends more on semiconductor supply capability.
Phase 1 encodes the owner thesis of strategic subsidy/capacity race before parity.
Owner thesis explicitly states a 3–5 year lag; triangular q12/q16/q20 encodes that uncertainty without selecting a point estimate.
Both systems accelerate equipment investment around parity.
Western localization response intensifies.
Strategic/defense procurement intensifies.
AI infrastructure spending remains elevated but more volatile.
Power buildout accelerates with duplicated compute systems.
Investment/fiscal intensity raises rate pressure.
Technology/export-control bifurcation reduces cross-border revenue.
Negative shift represents access friction/duplication risk, not loss of Taiwan strategic value.
Cheaper compute begins to pressure service pricing/economics.
Parity sharply increases accelerator price/performance competition.
Duplicated systems tightly couple compute and power investment.
Parity-boundary capex is supply capability dependent.
Technology capability and cross-border market access begin decoupling.
Phase 2 is deliberately volatile and temporary; it is the boundary the owner explicitly asked to study.

phases.name: Persistent Western and Chinese semiconductor systems

meta.rationale: Phase 3 starts after a four-quarter parity-boundary repricing window.
Duplicated supply chains keep equipment demand above BASE.
Strategic localization persists.
Defense/sovereign compute demand remains elevated.
Western AI buildout remains structurally above BASE.
Power infrastructure remains structurally elevated.
Rate pressure moderates but stays above BASE.
Cross-border technology revenue remains structurally impaired.
Supply-access friction remains; driver is not used as a proxy for Taiwan strategic relevance.
Cheaper non-Western chips pressure global compute service economics.
Sustained two-system competition compresses accelerator economics.
Persistent synchronized sovereign compute/power buildout.
Buildout remains supply-capability dependent.
Two production systems can improve local supply health while cross-border market access remains poor.
Persistent bifurcation, not an assumption that either bloc disappears.

fact_catalog.signal: SMIC/Chinese foundry disclosed process capability, production scale, yield or advanced-node revenue evidence narrowing the leading-edge gap.
preferred_sources: SMIC annual/interim reports and exchange filings
official Chinese industry disclosures where metric is explicit
fact_catalog.note: If yield/process metric is not separately disclosed, record not_disclosed; do not infer.

fact_catalog.signal: New or tightened U.S./allied semiconductor export controls affecting advanced compute, equipment or China market access.
Government semiconductor/AI infrastructure subsidies, awards or procurement commitments in U.S./EU/China.
preferred_sources: U.S. Department of Commerce CHIPS office
official Chinese central/provincial notices where quantified
fact_catalog.note: Track amount, beneficiary and effective date; announcement != disbursement.

fact_catalog.signal: China share of semiconductor equipment demand/revenue and evidence of domestic WFE substitution.
preferred_sources: ASML/AMAT/LRCX/KLAC issuer filings and earnings materials
fact_catalog.note: Use issuer-reported geography/segment facts; do not synthesize undisclosed market share.

fact_catalog.signal: Observed accelerator price/performance competition from Chinese suppliers or material price compression in comparable accelerator classes.
fact_catalog.note: This is the trigger family for ACCELERATOR_PRICE_COMPETITION; comparable product class must be explicit.

fact_catalog.signal: Material divergence of Western vs China semiconductor supply chains, including restricted cross-sales or duplicated fab capacity.
fact_catalog.note: Used for recalibration of bifurcation persistence, not for owner probability automatically.

notes: Owner thesis preserved in accompanying rationale verbatim.
TAIWAN_SUPPLY retains supply-health semantics; it is not redefined as Taiwan strategic value.
